# Fintech lenders

## Firmographics

Online lenders of fifty to four hundred people, based in the United States and
Canada, that make small business loans of ten thousand to two hundred and fifty
thousand dollars. Most are between their Series B and their Series D, and most
fund their loans from a warehouse line with one or two banks.

## Felt needs

Their credit teams cannot clear applications as fast as their marketing brings
them in. The material calls this "the queue on Monday morning", and it comes up
in every call note from the last quarter.

## Use cases

They read bank statements and tax returns into one view in minutes, decide on
the easy half of applications the same day, and send the hard half to a senior
underwriter with the reasons already written down.

## Current solutions

Two underwriters per hundred applications, a shared spreadsheet of decisions,
and a bank statement reader bought three years ago that nobody trusts.

## Team structure

A credit team of four to twelve people under a head of credit, a sales team of
two to six, and a marketing team of one or two.

## Trigger events

A new warehouse line, a new funding round, or a quarter where approvals fell
behind applications for the second time in a row.
